T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are unavailable.
detection_rules: Repeated authentication failures (>5 attempts) from single IP/user within short window
Failed authentication attempts followed immediately by a successful authentication from same source
recommendations: Immediately isolate or block source IP address at perimeter firewall
Enforce mandatory password reset and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) re-verification for affected user
Check active sessions for user account across all internal resources
Review domain controller authentication logs for additional password spray indicators

T1059.001.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1059.001.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution, stealthy downloaders, and fileless execution.
detection_rules: PowerShell process spawned by unusual parent application (e.g., winword.exe, excel.exe, cmd.exe)
Encoded command line execution (-Enc, -EncodedCommand, Base64 strings)
recommendations: Isolate target endpoint from network immediately
Decode and inspect Base64 command-line payload for malicious C2 domains or script blocks
Inspect parent process tree and document history for macro/exploit execution
Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104) across domain endpoints

T1046.name: Network Service Discovery
T1046.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts to identify potential targets for lateral movement.
detection_rules: Single source IP initiating connection attempts to >15 distinct destination ports within short time window
Sequential TCP SYN sweeps across internal IP subnets
recommendations: Identify target host performing scan and determine if host is compromised endpoint or authorized scanner
Review firewall and network access control lists (ACLs) to restrict internal subnet-to-subnet traffic
Check host for lateral movement tools (Nmap, Masscan, PortScan scripts)
Monitor internal network traffic for follow-on exploitation attempts on open ports

T1071.004.name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
T1071.004.description: Adversaries may communicate using the Domain Name System (DNS) protocol to convey command and control (C2) data or exfiltrate sensitive files.
detection_rules: High volume of DNS requests to non-standard, high-entropy or newly registered domains
Abnormally long DNS query domain lengths containing encoded subdomains
recommendations: Block target malicious domain at DNS resolver / perimeter firewall level
Inspect host memory and network traffic for DNS tunneling utilities (dnscat2, iodine)
Isolate compromised workstation and analyze recent process activity
Enforce internal DNS traffic through hardened corporate recursive DNS servers only

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts to log in to target environments from impossible geographic locations.
detection_rules: Logins for same account from geographically distant locations within timeframe impossible by physical travel (< 1 hour)
Concurrent active sessions originating from distinct ASN / ISP providers
recommendations: Revoke active session tokens and force immediate global logout for affected account
Prompt user to confirm current physical location and verify authorized activity
Check VPN and Identity Provider (IdP) logs for compromise indicators
Enable Conditional Access policies requiring MFA and compliant device posture

T1068.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
T1068.description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in attempts to elevate privileges on system components.
detection_rules: Sudden privilege escalation commands (sudo, runas) by non-privileged accounts
Execution of system binaries with elevated root rights
recommendations: Audit sudoers configuration file and user permissions
Isolate host workstation and check for local privilege escalation exploits

T1041.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
T1041.description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.
detection_rules: High volume HTTP POST upload events or binary transfers to external IPs
recommendations: Block destination IP on edge firewall
Perform DLP triage on exfiltrated dataset

T1190.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
T1190.description: Adversaries may attempt to take advantage of a weakness in an Internet-facing computer or program.
detection_rules: HTTP requests containing SQL injection or XSS payloads blocked by WAF
recommendations: Verify edge WAF rules
Audit web application code for input validation vulnerabilities
